name: Doji
description: A candle where the open and close are nearly equal, forming a cross or plus shape. Signals indecision between buyers and sellers. Its significance is entirely context-dependent — a doji after a long trend carries far more weight than one in consolidation.

body_rules.open_close_relationship: open and close are at or near the same price level
body_rules.body_to_range_ratio: body is less than 5% of the total candle range

wick_rules.symmetry: wicks can be equal (standard doji), long upper only (gravestone), long lower only (dragonfly), or both long (long-legged doji)

context_requirement: must appear after a prolonged trend (up or down) to signal a potential reversal; in ranging markets it is noise
volume_requirement: higher than average volume adds confirmation weight; low volume doji in a trend is less significant
agent_rules: Never act on a doji alone; always require confluence with support/resistance or a key level
A doji at resistance after an uptrend is bearish; at support after a downtrend is bullish
Wait for the next candle to confirm direction before entering
Gravestone doji (long upper wick) at resistance is a stronger bearish signal
Dragonfly doji (long lower wick) at support is a stronger bullish signal
Doji inside consolidation ranges should be ignored
